chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Al-Redha (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with two witnesses, then he reconciled with her, but did not have sexual intercourse with her after the reconciliation until she purified from her menstruation, then he divorced her again on a state of purity with two witnesses. Does the second divorce take effect upon her, having reconciled with her but not having had intercourse? He said: Yes.

key_terms.يُجَامِعۡهَا: he had sexual intercourse with her
key_terms.يُرَاجِعُهَا: he reconciled with her / took her back

ai.seo_question: Is sexual intercourse required for a second divorce to be valid after a revocable divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies a specific nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of the second divorce (talaq al-thani) in a revocable divorce (talaq al-raji'). He establishes that for the second divorce to be considered final and binding, the husband must have consummated the reconciliation through sexual intercourse during the waiting period (iddah); mere verbal reconciliation without intercourse is insufficient to validate the subsequent divorce.
